title: Not Every Mention Is a Claim: Rethinking Object Hallucination Detection in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.23610v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Object hallucination in vision-language models (VLMs) is usually measured by checking each object a caption names against the image. Most benchmarks and detectors alike treat every object mention as a claim that the object is present. This assumption fails when a caption names an object without asserting it, as in "a bench for people to sit on", which mentions people without claiming that any are in the image. We call such mentions non-assertive. Treating them as hallucinations inflates the error rates attributed to models that use such language. To separate them from real hallucinations, we introduce NAME-Bench (Non-Assertive Mention Evaluation Benchmark), 25,497 object mentions from captions that five VLMs generate for COCO images. Each mention is labelled concrete (asserted and present), hallucinated (asserted and absent), or non-assertive, and non-assertive mentions are further divided into four subtypes: depictive, purpose, negati

translated_title: 并非每个提及都是断言：重新思考视觉语言模型中的对象幻觉检测
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）中的对象幻觉通常通过将字幕中提到的每个对象与图像进行核对来衡量。大多数基准测试和检测器都将每个对象提及视为该对象存在的断言。当字幕提到一个对象但没有断言它时，这一假设就会失效，例如“供人们坐的长椅”提到了人，但并未断言图像中真的有人。我们将这类提及称为非断言性提及。将它们视为幻觉会夸大使用此类语言表达的模型所被归咎的错误率。为了将它们与真实的幻觉区分开来，我们引入了NAME-Bench（非断言性提及评估基准），该基准包含五个VLM为COCO图像生成的字幕中的25,497个对象提及。每个提及被标记为具体（已断言且存在）、幻觉（已断言但不存在）或非断言性，非断言性提及又进一步划分为四种子类型：描述性、目的性、否定性……
tldr: 该论文指出并非字幕中的每个对象提及都是存在性断言，并提出NAME-Bench基准，对25,497个对象提及进行标注以将非断言性提及与真实幻觉区分开，从而避免夸大视觉语言模型的幻觉错误率。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces NAME-Bench, which labels 25,497 object mentions as concrete, hallucinated, or non-assertive, showing that treating non-assertive mentions as hallucinations inflates error rates and calling for a rethinking of object hallucination detection in vision-language models.
